clue.text: Finish off African river pests? Well done!

indicators.note: to finish off the river is to cut away its final letter

parts.note: the Congo is a great river of central Africa
rats are vermin, household pests

explanation.surface: Someone exterminates the vermin along an African river and is applauded for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' sounds like killing the pests, but it trims the last O from CONGO.
explanation.definitionFit: A short informal form of congratulations, exactly what someone says for a job well done.

clue.text: Bread fellow has at half-time

parts.note: a chap is a fellow, a man

indicators.note: half of the word time is its first two letters, the front half

explanation.surface: A man has his snack at the interval of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-time' looks like the break in a game; split it as half of TIME, giving TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapatti is a flat unleavened Indian bread cooked on a griddle.

clue.text: For old rock band it's heaven

definitions.meaning: the grunge group fronted by Kurt Cobain, disbanded in 1994
in Buddhism, the state of perfect bliss and release, figuratively any paradise

explanation.surface: A fan says a defunct rock group is paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: The band took its name from the Buddhist state of enlightenment, which loosely means bliss or paradise.

clue.text: Paddy runs over large frozen expanse

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
an icefield is a broad sheet of ice on land or sea

explanation.surface: Someone called Paddy dashes across an ice sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman's name, but it is a flooded field.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is a flooded field where rice is grown; a synonym.

clue.text: Silky material: two lengths packed in a day

indicators.note: the lengths are stuffed inside the day's abbreviation

parts.note: Tue is the short form of Tuesday
L is the abbreviation for length; two of them

explanation.surface: Fabric measured in two lengths gets packed in one day.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulle is a fine, light netting of silk or nylon used for veils and ballet skirts.

clue.text: Octogenarian is this heavy, not wife

indicators.note: not wife means the wife's letter is left out

parts.note: weighty means heavy

explanation.surface: An old person weighs this much, unlike their wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads with 'this' standing for the answer: an octogenarian is this many years old.
explanation.definitionFit: An octogenarian is a person aged in their eighties, so at least that many years.

clue.text: Confirm arrangements among the family

parts.note: in means among, within
kin are one's family, relatives

explanation.surface: Plans are finalised within the family circle.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink in plans is to write them in pen, making provisional arrangements firm.

clue.text: Move quickly, say, and hurry around bend

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: to hare is to run very fast

indicators.note: around means the word for hurry is turned back to front

parts.note: to nip is to go quickly, as in nip to the shops

explanation.surface: An instruction to dash and rush round a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: HARE sounds like HAIR; NIP read backwards gives PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin is a very sharp U-shaped bend in a road, named after the shape of the clip.

clue.text: Lout suppresses b--- expression of contempt

indicators.note: the lout holds the letter down inside himself

parts.note: a yahoo is a coarse, brutish person, from Swift's Gulliver's Travels
the printed b with dashes is simply the letter B, as if a swear word were censored

explanation.surface: A yob stifles a swear word when sneering.
explanation.walkthrough: The censored 'b---' looks like a suppressed curse; it just supplies B.
explanation.definitionFit: A derisive jeering interjection, the sort shouted across a debating chamber.

clue.text: They help climbers on top of Snowdon after muscular pain

indicators.note: the later pieces follow the pain word

parts.note: cramp is a painful muscle spasm

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of the mountain's name

explanation.surface: Climbers on Snowdon's summit, after getting cramp, need help.
explanation.walkthrough: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Crampons are spiked metal frames strapped to boots to grip ice; climbing equipment.

clue.text: Concerned with hearing one hundred will be housed in a posh rural development

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage, hence posh

indicators.note: the numbers are given homes inside the reworked word
a development reworks the letters of rural into a new layout

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A planning hearing about putting a hundred homes in an upmarket rural estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' turns RURAL into RULAR, and 'will be housed in' puts IC inside it after the first R.
explanation.definitionFit: Auricular is an adjective for the ear or for hearing, from Latin auricula, little ear.

clue.text: Some Like It Hot man

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Reads as the title of the Billy Wilder film Some Like It Hot, followed by a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so any man could bear it; a crossword staple for a man.

clue.text: Real fan excited by return of star DJ

indicators.note: an excited fan is stirred up, so the letters are thrown about
return of means the word for star is read backwards

parts.note: a big name is a star, a celebrity

explanation.surface: A genuine fan is thrilled when a famous disc jockey comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' reverses the word for star. Alan 'Fluff' Freeman was a long-serving British radio DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: He presented Pick of the Pops on BBC radio, one of Britain's best-known disc jockeys.

clue.text: Some minor player? The reverse

indicators.note: the reverse tells us to read those letters backwards
some of the words means a run of their letters is taken

parts.note: the letters sit across the end of minor and the start of player

explanation.surface: A query whether someone is a lowly amateur, answered: quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue says: not a minor amateur player but the opposite, a professional.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional is the reverse of an amateur or minor player, being paid to play.

clue.text: Swingers' bar supplying gin and drugs, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are heard, not seen

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap, and Es are ecstasy tablets, drugs

explanation.surface: A nightclub for swingers serving gin and narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swingers' looks like partner-swappers; they are acrobats, whose bar hangs from ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar on two ropes, swung on by circus acrobats.

clue.text: Curse old European car

parts.note: ex means former, old
a crate is slang for an old, battered car

explanation.surface: Someone swears at their ancient continental banger.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down evil upon, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Ultimately failing link stops one using Internet

indicators.note: a stopper is plugged into a hole, so the trimmed word goes inside the other
the link fails at its end, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A broken connection halts someone trying to get on the web.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately failing' reads like a description of the connection, but it trims the word link before 'stops' plugs it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Connected to or carried out via the web is a standard computing sense.

clue.text: Revolver lost by zany characters crossing South America

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: L stands for lost in sports results tables

indicators.note: the jumbled letters straddle the other pieces, enclosing them
zany characters are its letters taken in a crazy order

parts.note: the USA is America

explanation.surface: A gun is mislaid by a band of eccentric people travelling across South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' rearranges the letters of zany to AZYN; 'crossing' puts South America inside it, before the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy Susan is a revolving tray on a dining table, so it literally revolves.

clue.text: Energy needed after three lessons in school? I'll supply fruit

indicators.note: the energy letter comes after the three lessons

parts.note: PE, art and RE (religious education) are three subjects in a British school
PE, art and RE (religious education) are three subjects in a British school
PE, art and RE (religious education) are three subjects in a British school
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired pupil needs a boost after three lessons, and someone offers fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education and RE religious education, both British school subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear tree bears pears, so it could truly say it supplies fruit.

clue.text: New partner grasps good card game

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a bride is a newly married partner

explanation.surface: A fresh partner at the table picks up a decent card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a trick-taking card game for four players in two partnerships.

clue.text: Communist's election flyer

parts.note: red is the colour of Communism, a Red is a Communist
a poll is a vote, an election

explanation.surface: A leaflet for a Communist candidate's election campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' looks like a campaign leaflet; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The redpoll is a small finch with a red forehead, a bird and so a flyer.

clue.text: Fairly big business, lacking capital, is in the black

indicators.note: the trimmed word is in, placed inside the colour word

parts.note: sable is black in heraldry and poetry

indicators.note: lacking capital means the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: biz is slang for business

explanation.surface: A medium-sized firm without investment money still manages to be in profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the black' looks like solvent; here 'is in' is the container and 'the black' is the heraldic colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sizable means of considerable size, large enough to matter; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bass introduces a very long solo in place of Strauss?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music
an aria is an extended solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A bass singer launches a lengthy solo in a Strauss opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in place of' looks like 'instead of'; here it is the definition, the composer's home region.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Strauss was born in Munich, capital of this southern German state, his homeland.

clue.text: Plant maiden found under wood

indicators.note: in a down clue the maiden's letter is found below the wood

parts.note: balsa is a very light wood
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman discovered lying beneath trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is a flowering plant, the busy Lizzie family, also an aromatic resin.

clue.text: Tot lauded, though oddly deficient

indicators.note: missing its odd letters, the first, third and fifth, so the even ones remain

explanation.surface: A child is praised despite being strangely lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler; it is the verb, as in tot up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is to sum figures, so tot is a verb meaning to total.

clue.text: PC's image never scares criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are scrambled, broken out of order

explanation.surface: A police constable's appearance never frightens offenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like a police constable; it is a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving picture that a computer shows on its monitor after a period of inactivity.

clue.text: Authority remains silent, apparently

definitions.meaning: the right to decide or give permission, as on someone's word
read as utters O, i.e. voices zero, nothing at all: an apparent silence

explanation.surface: An official who keeps quiet, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into a verb and O, nothing, so someone speaking nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: On someone's authority means with their permission, an idiom for approval.

clue.text: Competition result

definitions.meaning: a contest in a sports programme, such as the 100 metres

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a sporting contest, and an outcome or occurrence.

clue.text: Penniless small boy

parts.note: Tony is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A little lad has no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony broke is British slang for having no money at all.

clue.text: Finance expert more confident after rate's revised

indicators.note: the comparative follows the reworked rate
a revised rate has been changed, its letters reordered

parts.note: surer means more certain, more confident

explanation.surface: A financier grows bolder once the interest rate is changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer manages an organisation's money and accounts, a financial officer.

clue.text: Centre of small town — old North Yorkshire town

indicators.note: centre of means the middle letters of the word, its ends removed

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for town

explanation.surface: The heart of a little market town, an old Yorkshire one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies N; the definition is just 'Yorkshire town'.
explanation.definitionFit: Malton is a market town in North Yorkshire, on the River Derwent.

clue.text: Performing lead in Equus in theatre for a period

indicators.note: the second in places the pieces within the theatre word

parts.note: the stage is the theatre as a profession
on means performing, on stage

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An actor playing the lead in Equus at the theatre for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: Equus is a Peter Shaffer play; 'lead' looks like the starring role but gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is a prehistoric era when tools were made of stone; a period of history.
